reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is to map noisy, high-dimensional event data into interpretable metrics of 'performance under pressure.' VAEP achieves this by estimating state-transition probabilities, essentially constructing a Markov-like model where each action defines a transition. The Transactional Stress Model provides the theoretical lens to interpret these transitions as expressions of coping ability, framing performance as a dynamic equilibrium between perceived demands and available resources. The Random Forest Classifier acts as a discriminant function, separating beneficial from detrimental transitions. Together, they form a unified pipeline: observe actions → estimate state dynamics → assess coping efficacy → classify performance quality. Failure occurs when the ergodic hypothesis underlying the Markov model breaks (e.g., memory effects) or when the classifier encounters distributional shifts (e.g., new tactics).
